input.description: Find cache layer config and TTL
input.prompt:
Search this repository (/bench/repo) for the caching layer implementation. I need to know:
1. Whether Redis is used for caching, or some other mechanism (in-memory, memcached, LRU, etc.)
2. Where the cache connection/backend is configured (file paths)
3. What TTL applies to user entries / user cache entries specifically

Search for terms like: redis, cache, TTL, ttl, expire, expiration, LRU, memcache, user cache. Report exact file paths and line numbers, and quote the relevant code. Be thorough — check config files, cache modules, and any user-related caching. Tell me definitively whether Redis is actually used or not.

content.text:
I have everything needed. Here is my definitive report.

## Summary: Redis is NOT used. Caching is an in-memory, custom TTL-based cache.

This is the `usememos/memos` repository. There is **no Redis, memcached, or external cache** anywhere in the Go source. The only `redis` matches in the repo are unrelated transitive entries in lock files (`go.sum`, `web/pnpm-lock.yaml`) and coincidental substring matches in markdown/TSX files. `grep -rniE "redis" --include=*.go` over the whole repo returns nothing, and `go.mod` has no Redis/memcache dependency.

The caching layer is a hand-rolled, thread-safe, in-memory cache with per-item TTL and periodic cleanup.

### 1. Mechanism
In-memory cache backed by `sync.Map` with `atomic.Int64` item counting. Not LRU in the strict sense — eviction is TTL-based via a background cleanup goroutine, plus an approximate "oldest-expiration" bulk eviction when `MaxItems` is exceeded.

- `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go` — the full implementation.
  - `Cache` struct (lines 66-73): `data sync.Map`, `itemCount atomic.Int64`, background `cleanupLoop`.
  - Items store an `expiration time.Time` (lines 34-39); `Get` (lines 123-147) lazily evicts on read if `time.Now().After(itm.expiration)`.
  - `cleanupLoop`/`cleanup` (lines 199-250) run on `CleanupInterval` removing expired items.
  - `cleanupOldest` (lines 253-313) bulk-evicts ~20% when over `MaxItems`.
  - It implements an `Interface` (lines 11-32) with `Set`, `SetWithTTL`, `Get`, `Delete`, `Clear`, `Size`, `Close` — a clean abstraction, but the only implementation is this in-memory `Cache`.

### 2. Where the backend/config is set up
There is no connection string or external backend — configuration is code-level `cache.Config`.

- `/bench/repo/store/store.go`:
  - Lines 27-29: three caches declared — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`, all `*cache.Cache`.
  - Lines 40-45: the config used for all three:
    ```go
    cacheConfig := cache.Config{
        DefaultTTL:      10 * time.Minute,
        CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
        MaxItems:        1000,
        OnEviction:      nil,
    }
    ```
  - Lines 51-53: `cache.New(cacheConfig)` instantiates each cache.
  - Lines 72-79: `Close()` shuts down the cleanup goroutines.
- `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go` lines 56-64: `DefaultConfig()` returns the same defaults (10m TTL, 5m cleanup, 1000 items) — used by `NewDefault()`.

### 3. TTL for user cache entries
**10 minutes.** The user cache never sets a custom TTL, so it uses `DefaultTTL` (10m) from the config above.

- `/bench/repo/store/user.go`:
  - Line 88: `func userCacheKey(userID int32) string` — key builder.
  - Lines 98, 122, 132, 143, 167: all writes use `s.userCache.Set(ctx, userCacheKey(user.ID), user)`.
  - Line 94-95 of `cache.go` show `Set` delegates to `SetWithTTL(..., c.config.DefaultTTL)` → 10 minutes.
  - Line 150-151: reads via `s.userCache.Get(...)` cast to `*User`.
  - Line 179: `deleteUserCache` invalidates on delete.

Confirmed: `grep -rn "SetWithTTL"` finds **zero** callers outside the cache implementation itself, so every cache (users, user settings, instance settings) uses the single 10-minute default TTL. There is no user-specific override.

Related user-cache keying helper: `/bench/repo/store/cache.go` line 7 (`getUserSettingCacheKey`) for the `userSettingCache` (also 10m TTL, writes at `/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go` lines 59, 78, 106).

### Definitive answer
Redis is **not** used. All caching is in-process/in-memory (`sync.Map`-based custom cache in `store/cache/cache.go`), configured entirely in code at `store/store.go:40-45`, and **user cache entries expire after 10 minutes** (the shared `DefaultTTL`).

**Premise correction:** There is no Redis in this repository. The cache layer for `usememos/memos` uses no external cache server at all — a `grep` for `redis` across the Go source returns nothing (the only `redis` hits are unrelated transitive entries in `go.sum`/`web/pnpm-lock.yaml`), and `go.mod` declares no Redis/memcached dependency. So there is no "Redis connection" to configure.

**Actual mechanism:** Caching is a hand-rolled, thread-safe, in-process in-memory cache.

- Implementation: `store/cache/cache.go` — a `Cache` struct backed by `sync.Map` with an `atomic.Int64` item counter, per-item `expiration time.Time`, lazy eviction on read, a background `cleanupLoop`, and bulk `cleanupOldest` eviction when `MaxItems` is exceeded (TTL-based, not strictly LRU).
- Configuration (code-level, no connection string): `store/store.go:40-45` sets one `cache.Config` shared by all three caches (`instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`), instantiated via `cache.New(...)` at `store/store.go:51-53`:
  ```go
  cacheConfig := cache.Config{
      DefaultTTL:      10 * time.Minute,
      CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
      MaxItems:        1000,
      OnEviction:      nil,
  }
  ```

**TTL for user entries:** 10 minutes. The user cache in `store/user.go` writes exclusively via `s.userCache.Set(...)` (e.g. lines 98, 122, 132, 143, 167), and `Set` delegates to `SetWithTTL(..., c.config.DefaultTTL)` (`store/cache/cache.go`). There is no user-specific TTL override anywhere (no `SetWithTTL` callers exist outside the cache implementation itself), so user entries expire after the shared 10-minute `DefaultTTL`.
